The maximum of the graph gives

solutions.latex:
The object is at least 300 m high when $h \ge 300$.
$$\begin{aligned} -5t^2 + 80t &\ge 300 \\ t^2 - 16t + 60 &\le 0 &&(\text{divide by } -5,\ \text{reverse the inequality}) \\ (t-6)(t-10) &\le 0 \end{aligned}$$
The parabola $y=(t-6)(t-10)$ opens upwards, so it is at or below zero between its roots:
$$6 \le t \le 10$$
The time spent at 300 m or more is
$$10 - 6 = 4 \text{ seconds}$$
This agrees with the graph, where the curve meets $h=300$ at $t=6$ and $t=10$. This is option A.

parts.latex: Which of the following could represent the graph of $y = -x^2 + 1$?

solutions.latex:
The graph of $y=-x^2+1$ is a parabola, since $x$ is squared.

The coefficient of $x^2$ is negative, so it is concave down.

The $y$-intercept is found by letting $x=0$:
$$y=1$$
The $x$-intercepts are found by letting $y=0$:
$$\begin{aligned} -x^2+1 &= 0 \\ x^2 &= 1 \\ x &= \pm 1 \end{aligned}$$
So the graph is a concave down parabola with $y$-intercept $1$ and $x$-intercepts $-1$ and $1$. Only graph C has these features (A is a line, B is exponential, D is a hyperbola).

$$\therefore\ \text{the graph is C}$$

parts.latex: Which of the following is a parabola?

solutions.latex:
A parabola is the graph of a quadratic $y = ax^2 + bx + c$: a smooth U-shape with one turning point and a vertical axis of symmetry.

Option A has this shape, with its vertex on the $y$-axis above the $x$-axis.

Option B is a straight line, option C is an exponential curve (it has a horizontal asymptote and no turning point) and option D is a cubic curve (it has a point of inflection and is not symmetric about the $y$-axis).

So the parabola is option A.

4472.stem:
A publisher sells a book for $\$10$. At this price, 5000 copies of the book will be sold and the revenue raised will be $5000 \times 10 = \$50\,000$.

The publisher is considering increasing the price of the book. For every dollar the price of the book is increased, the publisher will sell 50 fewer copies of the book.

If the publisher charges $(10 + x)$ dollars for each book, a quadratic model for the revenue raised, $R$, from selling the books is

$$R = -50x^2 + 4500x + 50\,000.$$

A graph of this quadratic model for revenue is shown. A dashed line is used for values of $x$ which are not relevant to the practical context of this problem.

\exfigure{38_q35_1}

figures.cap: parabola of revenue R against x, roots at -10 and 100

parts.latex: By first finding a suitable value of $x$, find the price the publisher should charge for each book to maximise the revenue raised from sales of the book.
Find the value of the intercept of the parabola with the vertical axis.

solutions.latex:
The parabola is symmetric about its vertical axis of symmetry, which passes through the maximum, midway between the two $x$-intercepts. Hence the maximum revenue occurs at $x = 45$.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Price} &= 10 + 45 \\ &= \$55 \end{aligned}$$
The publisher should charge $\$55$ for each book.

Find the width and height of the rectangle which will give the greatest possible area of the cross-section.

The maximum area occurs at the highest point of the graph, where the width is $w=20$.

6357.stem:
An isosceles triangle has height $h$ centimetres. The area of the triangle, in square centimetres, is given by the formula $A = 0.5h^2 + 3h$ and is shown in the graph below.

\exfigure{1247_q28_1}

figures.cap: parabola A = 0.5h^2 + 3h

parts.latex: Explain why only a certain part of this graph can be used to model the area of the triangle.
Calculate the perimeter of the triangle when the area is $8\ \text{cm}^2$. Give your answer correct to one decimal place.

solutions.latex: The height and area cannot be negative, so only the part of the graph with $h>0$ can be used.

Set $A=8$ in $A=0.5h^2+3h$:
$$\begin{aligned} 0.5h^2+3h &= 8 \\ h^2+6h-16 &= 0 \\ (h+8)(h-2) &= 0 \end{aligned}$$
so $h=2$ (a height is positive). Then $A=\dfrac12bh$ gives $8=\dfrac12 b(2)$, so $b=8$.

Each equal side $x$ is the hypotenuse of a right-angled triangle with sides $2$ and $4$ (half the base):
$$x^2=2^2+4^2$$
so $x=\sqrt{20}$.
$$\begin{aligned} P &= \sqrt{20}+\sqrt{20}+8 \\ &= 16.9 \text{ cm} \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Finds the slant side, or equivalent merit
Finds the height $h=2$, or equivalent merit

6384.stem:
Chloe plans to build a rectangular enclosure for her new chickens against an existing wall, using 16 metres of wire fencing as shown below. She calls the dimensions of the enclosure $x$ and $y$.

\exfigure{308_q24_1}

figures.cap: enclosure against existing wall, sides x, x, y
parabola A = 16x - 2x^2

parts.latex: She reasons that $2x + y = 16$. Write $y$ in terms of $x$ and hence, show that the area of the enclosure can be written as $A = 16x - 2x^2$.
parts.note: Forming a quadratic model (area) from a description

parts.latex: Determine the dimensions (both $x$ and $y$) that will achieve the maximum possible area for the enclosure.

solutions.latex:
The wall forms one side, so the fence is two sides of length $x$ and one of length $y$. The wire is 16 m.
$$\begin{aligned} 2x+y &= 16 \\ y &= 16-2x \end{aligned}$$
The area of the rectangle is $A=xy$.
$$\begin{aligned} A &= x(16-2x) \\ &= 16x-2x^2 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ y=16-2x \text{ and } A=16x-2x^2$$

Draw the horizontal line $A=24$ on the graph. It meets the curve where $x=2$ and where $x=6$.

Check: $16(2)-2(2)^2=24$ and $16(6)-2(6)^2=24$.

Find $y$ from $y=16-2x$.
$$\begin{aligned} x=2:\quad y &= 16-4=12 \\ x=6:\quad y &= 16-12=4 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ x=2 \text{ m with } y=12 \text{ m, or } x=6 \text{ m with } y=4 \text{ m}$$
criteria: Finds both values of $x$ ($2$ and $6$), or equivalent merit

meta.self_check: Substituted both x into A and y.

solutions.latex:
The graph is a parabola, so the maximum area occurs at its highest point, where $x=4$ (midway between the $x$-intercepts $0$ and $8$).
$$\begin{aligned} y &= 16-2(4) \\ &= 8 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ x=4 \text{ m and } y=8 \text{ m, giving the maximum area of } 32 \text{ m}^2$$

Labels x, x and y in maths italic; 'Fenced Enclosure' at the crop's position. Original score is just under 0.85 because the scan's strokes are thicker. Rules 1,3,19.

An object is thrown in the air. It takes 5 seconds for it to reach the ground. The height of the object is given by the formula:

$$h=-t^2+4t+5$$

When is the maximum height reached?
What was the initial height of the object?

solutions.latex: \extable{Ts9978_1}
\exfigure{821_q31_s1}

The maximum height is the greatest value of $h$ on the graph.

$$h_{\max} = 9 \text{ m}$$

meta.format_note: Rubric written by us. Units assumed metres.

solutions.latex:
The maximum occurs at the vertex, $t = -\dfrac{b}{2a} = -\dfrac{4}{-2} = 2$.

$$\therefore\ t = 2 \text{ seconds}$$

The initial height is at $t = 0$.

$$h = -0^2 + 4(0) + 5 = 5$$

$$\therefore\ \text{initial height} = 5 \text{ m}$$

parts.latex:
To determine the maximum area ($A$) of a rectangle with a perimeter of 30 m, Melanie sketched the following diagrams in her notebook.

\exfigure{823_q15_1}

The point $A$ is the turning point on the parabolic graph.

Melanie correctly determined the maximum area of the rectangle (in square metres) by finding the value of $A$.

What is the value?

solutions.latex:
With perimeter 30 m, the sides are $x$ and $15-x$.
$$A=x(15-x)=-x^2+15x$$
The maximum is at the vertex, $x=\dfrac{15}{2}=7.5$.
$$\begin{aligned} A &= -(7.5)^2+15(7.5) \\ &= 56.25 \end{aligned}$$
So the answer is C.

6757.stem:
A ball is thrown upward from a raised platform. The path of the ball's trajectory is modelled by $h=-0.001d^2+0.2d+30$ where $h$ is the height above the ground and $d$ is the horizontal distance the ball travels. A graph of the equation is shown below.

\exfigure{827_q41_1}

figures.cap: parabola of h against d

parts.latex: From what height is the ball thrown?
What is the maximum distance above the ground the ball reaches?
What is the horizontal distance travelled?
What is the height when $d=215.2$?

solutions.latex:
The ball is thrown at $d=0$.
$$h=30 \text{ m}$$

Read the maximum height from the graph.
$$\therefore\ 40 \text{ m}$$

Read the horizontal distance where the ball lands ($h=0$) from the graph.
$$\therefore\ 300 \text{ m}$$

Substitute $d=215.2$ into the model:
$$\begin{aligned} h &= -0.001(215.2)^2+0.2(215.2)+30 \\ &\approx 26.7 \text{ m} \end{aligned}$$

The grid copies the paper: grey major lines every 50 in d and 5 in h, fine dotted minor lines every 10 in d and 1 in h, from d=-200 to 400 and h=-5 to 45. Axes have arrows. parts.latex: Which of the following graph best represents the equation $y = x^2 + 3$?

solutions.latex:
The coefficient of $x^2$ is positive, so the parabola is concave up (opens upward). This rules out options C and D.

When $x=0$, $y=3$, so the $y$-intercept is above the $x$-axis. This rules out option A, which crosses the $y$-axis below the $x$-axis.

Also $x^2+3\ge 3>0$ for all $x$, so the curve never meets the $x$-axis. Option B is concave up, has a minimum at $(0,3)$ and has no $x$-intercepts.

Find the exact height of the ball when its height is at a maximum.
Give, with reasons, one range of $x$ values for which this model will not be practical.

solutions.latex:
The initial height is $h$ when $x=0$.
$$h = 3.75$$
$$\therefore\ \text{initial height} = 3.75 \text{ m}$$

The graph is symmetric about its maximum, which lies midway between the $x$-intercepts $x=-3$ and $x=25$.
$$x = \dfrac{-3 + 25}{2} = 11$$
$$\begin{aligned} h &= 3.75 + 1.1(11) - 0.05(11)^2 \\ &= 9.8 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{maximum height} = 9.8 \text{ m}$$
criteria: Indicates that the maximum height occurs when $x=11$, on the graph or numerically, or equivalent merit

meta.format_note: Intercepts $-3$ and $25$ read from the given graph.

solutions.latex:
$x<0$ is not practical, because the ball starts at $x=0$.

OR

$x>25$ is not practical, because then the height would be below $0$.

parts.latex: Which table of values matches the relationship $y = x^2 - 2$

solutions.latex:
Substitute each $x$ value into $y = x^2 - 2$.
$$\begin{aligned} x=-1:\quad y &= (-1)^2 - 2 = -1\\ x=0:\quad y &= 0^2 - 2 = -2\\ x=1:\quad y &= 1^2 - 2 = -1\\ x=2:\quad y &= 2^2 - 2 = 2 \end{aligned}$$
The table of values is $y = -1,\ -2,\ -1,\ 2$, which matches option A.

The other options each have a wrong value (for example $-3$ at $x=-1$ or $2$ at $x=0$).
